the DNA from the antibody-forming cells contains unique genes coding for immunoglobin polypeptide chains.
the spleen of the immunized animal contains a greater proportion of genes coding for the immunoglobulin polypetide chains than does the liver.

the DNA of lymphoid tissues contains a larger proportion of genes that are unique or redundant to those of liver than of spleen DNA, and that the RNA of lymphoid tissue contains a larger proportion that is complementary to spleen DNA than to liver DNA.

the molecular biology of antibody formation.
